# Sourcify

This file provides an overview of the Sourcify API documentation.

## Bulk access and fair use (read this first)

The Sourcify API serves single contracts. It is not for bulk downloads. Do not crawl it.

### Pick the right source

- Many contracts, or the full dataset: use the Parquet export. It is free and updated daily. Docs: https://docs.sourcify.dev/docs/repository/download-dataset/
- Analytics without a download: query the Parquet files remotely with DuckDB (see below).
- SQL with many lookups by address, without a download: use the public BigQuery dataset. It is updated continuously. You need a Google account. Docs: https://docs.sourcify.dev/docs/bigquery/
- One contract, or a few contracts: use the API (see below).

To download the full Parquet dataset and keep it in sync, run this command. On later runs, it downloads only new or changed files.

```bash
aws s3 sync s3://sourcify-production-parquet-export/v2/ ./sourcify-dataset --endpoint-url https://storage.googleapis.com --no-sign-request
```

For current file counts and sizes, see https://export.sourcify.dev/v2/stats.json.

### Query the Parquet files without downloading

DuckDB can query the files in place. It reads only the parts that a query needs. No credentials are needed.

```sql
INSTALL httpfs;
LOAD httpfs;
CREATE SECRET sourcify_export (TYPE s3, PROVIDER config, KEY_ID '', SECRET '', ENDPOINT 'storage.googleapis.com', URL_STYLE 'path');

SELECT chain_id, count(*) AS deployments
FROM 's3://sourcify-production-parquet-export/v2/contract_deployments/*.parquet'
GROUP BY chain_id
ORDER BY deployments DESC;
```

- Use the `s3://` form for all files of a table. HTTPS URLs do not support wildcards.
- Remote queries are fast for counts, aggregations, and filters on a few columns.
- Remote lookups by address are slow. The files are ordered by `created_at`, so one lookup reads about 1 GB.
- For many lookups by address, download the tables once, or use BigQuery.
- For one contract, use the API.

### Rules for API clients

- Do not loop over `/v2/contract/{chainId}/{address}` to collect many contracts. Use the dataset.
- Request only the fields that you need, for example `fields=abi` or `fields=sources`.
- Do not use `fields=all` in loops. It returns every field, including all source files. It is the most expensive request.
- Store responses. Do not fetch the same contract again.
- Send a descriptive `User-Agent` header. Name your tool or project, its version, and a contact URL or email. Example: `User-Agent: my-indexer/1.2 (+https://example.com; ops@example.com)`. Do not send a generic default such as `python-requests` or `curl`. This lets us contact you before we limit your traffic.
- Requests are rate limited per client. If you get a `429` or `5xx` response, stop and wait.
- Retry with exponential backoff. If the response has a `Retry-After` header, wait at least that long.
- Do not use `/v2/verify/etherscan` to import many contracts. Use it only for the contracts that you need.
- If the dataset does not fit your use case, email hello@sourcify.dev.

## Sourcify API versions:

- v1 (deprecated; don't use it)
- v2 (preferred; choose this)

## API specification (use this URL):

https://sourcify.dev/server/api-docs/swagger.json

### How to read the swagger file

The `swagger.json` file above is structured as follows:

```json
{
    "openapi": "OPENAPI_VERSION",
    "info": {
        "version": "SOURCIFY_VERSION",
    },
    "servers": [
        { "url": "https://sourcify.dev/server", "description": "Production server" },
        ...
    ],
    "paths": {
        "SOURCIFY_API_PATH": {
            "HTTP_METHOD": { /* OPENAPI SPECIFICATIONS */ }
        }
    }
}
```

### To verify smart contracts read

- paths["/v2/verify/{chainId}/{address}"].post

### Check verification job status

- paths["/v2/verify/{verificationId}"].get

### To read smart contracts read

- paths["/v2/contract/{chainId}/{address}"].get

## Contract deletion

The deployer of a verified contract can ask Sourcify to delete the verification data of the contract, source code included. These two endpoints are not in the swagger file. A Sourcify maintainer approves or rejects each request, so a deletion is not immediate.

- Only the deployer can ask. The deployer is `deployment.deployer` of `GET https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/{chainId}/{address}?fields=deployment`: the sender of the transaction that created the contract, also if a factory created it.
- Never ask a user for a private key. Give the user the message, and let the user sign it with a wallet (`personal_sign`, EIP-191).
- If Sourcify has no deployer for the contract, or the user cannot sign with the deployer account, the user writes to hello@sourcify.dev.

### Message to sign

Lines end with one line feed. The last line has no line end.

```
Sourcify contract deletion request

I am the deployer of the contracts below. I ask Sourcify to delete their verification data, source code included.

Service: sourcify-contract-deletion
Version: 3
Issued at: {issuedAt}
Contracts ({number of contracts}):
{chainId}:{address}
```

- One line `{chainId}:{address}` for each contract, sorted by chain id (as a number), then by address. Addresses in lower case. No duplicates. At most 50 contracts.
- `{issuedAt}` is the current UTC time in the form `2026-01-31T12:00:00Z` (no milliseconds). The request must arrive not later than 15 minutes after it.

### Send the request

`POST https://sourcify.dev/server/delete` with a JSON body. The contracts and the time must be the same as in the signed message:

```json
{
  "contracts": [{ "chainId": 1, "address": "0xae519fc2ba8e6ffe6473195c092bf1bae986ff90" }],
  "issuedAt": "2026-01-31T12:00:00Z",
  "signature": "0x..."
}
```

- `202`: `{"requestId": "<uuid>", "state": "pending"}`.
- Errors have the form `{"error": "<code>", "message": "<text>"}`. Codes: `invalid_request`, `not_canonical`, `too_many_contracts`, `request_expired`, `issued_in_future`, `invalid_signature` (400); `not_deployer` (403); `request_pending` (409, the deployer has a request that is not finished); `not_verified`, `unsupported_chain` (422); `unavailable` (503).

### Read the state

`GET https://sourcify.dev/server/delete/{requestId}` gives `{"requestId": "<uuid>", "state": "<state>"}`. The state is `pending`, `done`, `rejected`, `expired`, or `failed`. Do not poll more often than once in a minute: a maintainer decides, and that can take days. A request without a decision expires after 14 days.

### After a deletion

- Source files that other verified contracts also use stay in Sourcify with those contracts.
- The deletion does not stop a new verification of the same contract.

## Repository UI

Contract's data can be viewed in the web application at https://repo.sourcify.dev/{chainId}/{address}.

- Do not use this repository to retrieve individual files.
- LLMs should not use this repository for data exploration; use the API referenced above instead.
- You may share links to this repository with users who want to browse contract's data through the UI.
